evidence: Workbook row 2 (both sheets): 'Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.' Skill quality-checks.md section 2: verify 'sentence variety, contractions, the occasional terse fragment in the notes'; defect is 'uniform cadence, marketing gloss ("seamless", "robust", "delve"), perfectly parallel bullets, or a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes'. The template instruction.md is only the CHANGE_ME placeholder, so it sets no voice to preserve. task/instruction.md (683 bytes, sha256 4848dc69..., three short paragraphs) is first person and personal: line 1 'I'd like a small local playground', 'I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source', 'I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first'; line 5 'I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in.' Sentence length varies (4-word clause 'The editor itself matters' through a 26-word sentence), there is a contraction, and the motivation is a concrete personal habit rather than a feature pitch. A grep of instruction.md and all six notes for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|comprehensive|intuitive|ensure|utilize|streamline|powerful|elegant|additionally|furthermore|moreover and for em dashes returned zero hits; there are zero bullet or numbered-list lines in any of the seven files, so no parallel-bullet pattern. The notes keep the same speaker: overview.md:3 'while I work'; behaviour.md:11 'That refresh must not touch what I'm doing ... keep my draft; do not load the newer revision over my work'; ui.md:3 'Don't use a textarea ... and don't use CodeMirror', 'the source I see', ui.md:9 'however slowly', 'whichever you prefer'; integration.md:1 heading 'How I start the app', :3 'I start it with node /app/server.js'; policy.md:1 heading 'Choices left to you', :3 'A parser or formatter library is fine'. Terse sentences occur in the notes ('Save source as text.' security.md:5; 'A restored picture may be static.' behaviour.md:5; 'Navigation wraps at the ends.' ui.md:11). Notes, not defects: (a) the notes are markedly denser and more normative than the brief - 'must' appears 21 times across the notes (10 in behaviour.md) and never in instruction.md, and passages such as behaviour.md:3 ('Errors go to that same console: show a useful error message there with a one-based line number for a thrown error, including an error inside a complete HTML file, counted from the first line of that file, and a Promise rejection that nothing handles; ...') and ui.md:9 read as accreted requirement clauses rather than speech; this is a register shift toward precision, but the speaker, person and plain vocabulary stay the same, so it does not reach the skill's 'voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes' defect; (b) policy.md and security.md contain no first-person reference at all and security.md is the most impersonal of the notes; (c) 'useful' is reused as a stock qualifier (useful error, useful conflict feedback, useful formatting error, useful tool); (d) contractions are sparse outside the brief (I'm once, Don't/don't once each). Tried alternatives: a robotic rewrite ('The application shall provide ...', bulleted acceptance list, 'seamless editing experience') would fail this row and none of those markers is present; a terse casual human brief would pass and the current brief is already in that range. No run or scripted result in raw-evidence-index.json measures prose voice, and none is needed for this row; the judgement rests on the frozen text.
